subject: FinTechCo RTBF / deletion workflow - post-demo questions
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: FinTechCo RTBF / deletion workflow - post-demo questions

Hi Alex - great to meet earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a few follow-ups from our discovery call focused on data handling and deletion (RTBF):

Summary of what I heard:
- FinTechCo stores customer PII (name, email, account id) and transaction metadata; needs strict controls around deletion and evidence of purge.
- Primary requirement: ability to surface and delete a customer's personal data on demand and provide verification for procurement/legal.
- Retention constraints: corporate retention policy references up to 7 years for transaction records, but product/legal are evaluating exceptions for personal data.

Questions / items we need to confirm for the M.A.P.:
1) Which data elements do you consider PII for deletion requests (please confirm the exact fields / table names if possible)?
2) Expected SLA for user-initiated deletion of live data (we discussed 24-48h for the primary dataset - confirm your expectation).
3) Backups & snapshots: any legal/regulatory constraints that prevent deletion from backups within X days? What is your maximum acceptable purge window for backups?
4) Audit evidence: will a signed statement + deletion logs be sufficient, or do you need a 3rd-party cert / on-demand access to (redacted) records?
5) Data residency: do deletion requests need to be handled in-region (US-only) or is cross-region processing acceptable?

Next steps I propose:
- I'll pull together a short RTBF options summary (mechanics, trade-offs, typical timelines) and a draft SOW language for procurement.
- If you can, please send the list of PII fields and the internal retention policy excerpts that drive the 7-year requirement.

Attached: redwood-rtbf-overview.pdf (one-page process + options).

Thanks - happy to jump back on a quick call if helpful.

Camila Reyes

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>

Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinTechCo RTBF / deletion workflow - post-demo questions

Thanks Camila - useful recap. A few quick answers while we align internally:

1) PII scope: name, email, phone, account_id, government_id (rare), and any free-form notes on the customer profile. Transaction metadata (timestamps, amounts) is considered transactional, not PII, but is subject to retention.
2) SLA: Ideally our business wants confirmation of deletion from live systems within 24 hours; we understand backups are harder.
3) Backups & snapshots: Our legal team prefers purge from backups within 30 days of request if possible; however procurement expects to see exact mechanics. We have immutable snapshots for month-end archival - unclear whether those have to be retained for accounting.
4) Audit evidence: procurement wants an auditable deletion log + a short letter from Redwood confirming process and timelines; 3rd-party cert is nice-to-have but not required for initial procurement.
5) Data residency: must remain US-only processing for deletion actions and logs (we have EU customers but this specific contract will be US-only).

Attaching our high-level RTBF requirements doc: fintechco-rtbf-requirements.pdf. Legal is on CC (feel free to loop in compliance folks at Redwood).

Appreciate the options summary - looking forward to the SOW language.

-Alex

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: FinTechCo RTBF / deletion workflow - post-demo questions

Hi Alex / Camila - looping in Dylan from infra. Thanks for the clear answers, Alex - below is a proposed approach and the trade-offs so we can get aligned for procurement and the SOW.

Proposed RTBF mechanics (options):
A) Live-data deletion (recommended flow)
  - Soft-delete + async purge from primary DBs: confirm within 24 hours (we can mark records as deleted and remove from live indexes).
  - Deletion logs: we can emit an immutable audit record (deletion request id, requester, timestamp, affected objects) and provide a signed statement for procurement.

B) Backups & snapshots (trade-offs)
  - Standard backups: depending on your backup cadence (daily incremental, weekly full), purging deleted rows from backups requires either waiting for retention expiry or performing a rebuild/purge operation. Typical safe windows we see: 30-90 days.
  - Immutable monthly snapshots: if your accounting requires month-end immutable archives, those may need a retention exception; two options: (1) accept a legal note explaining the exception; or (2) use crypto-erase where we rotate/destroy the encryption key for those snapshots to render data unrecoverable - this provides a faster purge path but procurement/legal need to approve.

C) Faster purge option (if you need <30 days for backups)
  - Crypto-erase for encrypted backups (fast, but requires agreement on key management and proof-of-destruction workflow).
  - For certain customer tables we can maintain separate per-customer encryption keys (best for fast purges).

D) Residency & processing
  - We can run deletion operations and store deletion logs in US-only regions for this contract.

Next steps / asks from FinTechCo:
- Confirm accepted maximum window for backups (30 vs 90 days).
- Confirm whether immutable month-end snapshots must be retained and for how long for accounting/legal.
- If <60 days is required, confirm willingness to adopt crypto-erase and provide KMS integration points.

Internal next steps (for Redwood):
- Dylan: can you draft a short technical appendix describing our crypto-erase option and the expected timelines for per-customer key rotation?
- Camila: I'll work with you on SOW language and the deletion SLA clause. I'll attach a quick options summary.

Attached: rtbf-options-summary.txt (short bullet list).

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Compliance Integrations | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>

Thanks Neha - that aligns with procurement's expectations. Quick answers:
- We can accept up to 30 days maximum for backups if crypto-erase is available and you can provide a clear KMS/key-destruction workflow we can include in the SOW.
- Month-end immutable snapshots: accounting needs to retain for 7 years, but they are open to a legal exception for personal data if a certified crypto-erase statement is provided.

Request for next deliverables (procurement asks):
1) A short one-page statement describing the deletion flow + crypto-erase proof-of-destruction process we can attach to the procurement packet.
2) Draft SOW language including the 24-hour live deletion SLA and 30-day backup purge commitment (with the crypto-erase clause).
3) Example API call / support flow for initiating an RTBF request (we'll want to wire into our admin panel).

Camila - can you share the SOW draft + one-pager this week? If you can get Dylan's appendix on crypto-erase, we can circulate to legal/procurement and move to commercial review.

Thanks - Alex
